ledger.sentence: The NHS in England invites people with a cervix aged 25 to 64 for cervical screening.
ledger.note: GOV.UK/NHS: screening moves to five-yearly for ages 25 to 64 in England. "First invitation a few months before 25th birthday" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Routine screening is every five years.
ledger.note: GOV.UK: HPV-negative people are offered screening again in 5 years.

ledger.sentence: From 1 July 2025 in England, people who test negative for HPV are offered screening again after five years rather than three; guidance says some people last invited before that date may still be on a three-year interval.
ledger.note: GOV.UK: UK NSC recommended five-year intervals for 25 to 64; HPV-negative people last invited before 1 July 2025 may still be on a three-year interval; first-ever HPV-negative test at 25 means next test in 5 years. The "25 to 49 moved" description was not seen verbatim. NHS page text itself not retr

ledger.sentence: Cervical screening is usually done by a female nurse or doctor, and a person can ask for a female practitioner when booking.
ledger.note: Cancer Research UK: usually done by a female nurse or doctor and a person can ask for a female practitioner when booking. "Most at a GP surgery" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: The clinician gently places a tool called a speculum in the vagina and uses a soft brush to collect cells from the cervix.
ledger.note: Speculum and soft brush supported; "smooth, tube-shaped" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: One source says the test itself should take less than five minutes, and the whole appointment usually lasts 10 to 15 minutes.
ledger.note: Cancer Research UK: test itself should take less than 5 minutes; appointment usually 10 to 15 minutes. "About ten minutes" differs.

ledger.sentence: People can ask for a smaller speculum or ask to insert the speculum themselves.
ledger.note: Smaller speculum and inserting it yourself are supported; "ask to stop at any time" is not in retrieved text.

ledger.sentence: Light spotting for a few hours afterwards is normal.
ledger.note: Cancer Research UK: some spotting or light bleeding is very common and should go away after a few hours; bleeding that is not a period or after sex should be checked by a GP.

ledger.sentence: Current NHS practice tests the sample for high-risk HPV first.
ledger.note: NHS programme page: sample tested for HPV; HPV-positive samples get cytology triage.

ledger.sentence: The NHS England guide says high-risk HPV can cause abnormal cell changes that may lead to cervical cancer.
ledger.note: NHS programme page: most HPV infections are transient; persistent HPV can lead to abnormal cells that may become cancer if untreated. Attribution to the "NHS England guide" specifically not confirmed.

ledger.sentence: If HPV is found, the laboratory then looks more closely at the cells for changes.
ledger.note: GOV.UK: HPV-positive samples undergo cytology triage to see whether HPV has caused abnormal cell changes.

ledger.sentence: If HPV is not found, the person is offered screening again in five years.
ledger.note: Retrieved text says HPV negative means screening again in 5 years; "risk very low" and "usually" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: If HPV is found but the cells are normal, the person is usually retested in about 12 months.
ledger.note: GOV.UK: HPV-positive with negative cytology are offered yearly surveillance.

ledger.sentence: If HPV is found with abnormal cells, the person is referred for a colposcopy.
ledger.note: GOV.UK: abnormal cells with HPV lead to referral to colposcopy.

ledger.sentence: If more tests are needed, the results letter says what to do next.
ledger.note: Search found no text on unclear results; a "does not mean anything is wrong" reassurance is unsafe unsourced. Cancer Research UK: the result letter tells you what to do if more tests are needed.

ledger.sentence: Results are sent by letter or given by telephone, and the letter says what to do if more tests are needed.
ledger.note: Results by letter or telephone call (Cancer Research UK); no timeframe retrieved.

ledger.sentence: A colposcopy is the usual next step after an abnormal screening result.
ledger.note: Colposcopy is the usual next step after an abnormal result (research text); "hospital or clinic" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Cancer Research UK says cervical screening is not a test for cancer; it looks for HPV and cell changes.
ledger.note: No NHS text retrieved. A single Turkish study found CIN2 or worse in 13.5% of biopsies, not an NHS statement.

ledger.sentence: A biopsy is examined by a pathologist, who grades any cell changes as CIN1, CIN2 or CIN3.
ledger.note: Biopsy graded as CIN1, CIN2, CIN3 by a pathologist (research text). Treatment statements not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Cancer Research UK advises that bleeding between periods, after sex or after the menopause, or unusual discharge, should be checked by a GP.
ledger.note: Cancer Research UK advises contacting the GP practice as soon as possible after bleeding between periods, after sex or after the menopause, or unusual discharge. The "because" causal clause not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: The NHS in England invites people with a cervix aged 25 to 64 for cervical screening.
ledger.note: GOV.UK: five-year intervals for 25 to 64 in England.

ledger.sentence: The sample is tested first for high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), the virus that can lead to cell changes.
ledger.note: NHS programme page: samples tested for HPV, persistent HPV can lead to cell changes.

ledger.sentence: A negative HPV result means the person is offered screening again in five years.
ledger.note: HPV negative means screening again in five years (supported); "risk very low" not retrieved.

ledger.sentence: Cancer Research UK says cervical screening is not a test for cancer; it looks for HPV and cell changes.
ledger.note: No NHS text retrieved (see c23).

ledger.sentence: The NHS describes cervical screening as a test of the health of the cervix that helps to prevent cervical cancer, rather than a test for cancer.
ledger.note: NHS: 'not a test for cancer, it's a test to help prevent cancer'; checks the health of the cervix.

ledger.sentence: The NHS says screening is still important for people who have had the HPV vaccine.
ledger.note: NHS England: if you've had the HPV vaccine it is still important to attend; vaccine does not protect against all HPV types.

ledger.sentence: Booking is usually through the GP surgery, online or in the NHS App, and some sexual health clinics also offer it.
ledger.note: Usually via GP surgery; some areas offer sexual health clinics or walk-in centres; online via NHS App or by phone.

ledger.sentence: The NHS suggests wearing something that can stay on during the test, such as a skirt or long top, and bringing someone for support.
ledger.note: Guide: may want something to leave on like a long jumper, dress or skirt; can bring a friend, relative, partner or support worker.

ledger.sentence: The NHS says the person can ask to stop at any time and can ask for adjustments, such as a smaller speculum or a different position, to feel more comfortable.
ledger.note: Guide says say if you feel pain, ask for adjustments (smaller speculum, different position) and ask to stop at any time. 'Some find it uncomfortable' not stated in retrieved text.
